subject: Bar colour derived from comparison with another bar

messages.author: 4024e1d3d6b890f6
messages.subject: Bar colour derived from comparison with another bar
parts:
I'm charting some test results against a standard, or benchmark. There are a number of tests in the suite, and each run of tests results in some tests meeting or exceeding a per-test benchmark ("pass") and some not ("fail"). I'm producing the charts as a facet_wrap.

I'd like to change the colour of the bars in the chart such that
  • the standard bar is always black (or any invariant colour)
  • a bar that is less than or equal to the standard is green
  • a bar that is greater than the standard is red

Ideally, I'd like a legend to appear with title "Result", green fill = "pass" and red fill = "green", and I could put up with another entry of black fill = "standard".

Really ideally, I'd like the standard as a horizontal line across the chart instead of a bar and if I could do that I'd probably colour it other than black.

Suggestions on how to accomplish any or all of this would be greatly appreciated.

Example data, script and output attached.

regards - David

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: Bar colour derived from comparison with another bar
parts:
Hi David,
Here is one way:

dm$Result <- "pass"
dm <- ddply(dm, .(Test), function(DF) {
DF[which(DF$value > DF[DF$variable == "Std", "value"]),
"Result"] <- "fail"
DF[DF$variable == "Std", "Result"] <- "standard"
return(DF)
})


p <- qplot(x = variable, y = value, data = dm, geom = "bar", stat =
"identity", fill=Result) + opts(aspect.ratio = 1,
axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=45, hjust=1))

p1 <- p + facet_wrap(~ Test, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y")
p2 <- p1 + scale_colour_manual(values = c("red","blue", "green"))

print(p2)

best,
Ista

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Bar colour derived from comparison with another bar
parts:
Currently, the easiest way to get the colours is to train the scale yourself:

x <- factor(1:3)

col <- scale_colour_hue()
col$train(x, FALSE)
col$output_set()

In the future, I hope to pull out the essence of scaling into its own
package, so accessing the underlying algorithms is much easier.

Hadley

Hadley,

I'm probably being a bit dense here ... what do I do with col$output_set()?

I tried the code below and changing this line:
p2 <- p1 + scale_fill_manual(values = c("red","blue", "green"))
to this:
p2 <- p1 + scale_fill_manual(values = col$output_set())

which gets me the colours I was after but out of sequence. By inserting them manually like this:
p2 <- p1 + scale_fill_manual(breaks = c("standard", "pass", "fail"), values = c("fail" = "#F8766D", "pass" = "#00BA38", "standard" = "#619CFF"))

I get the colours I want, and the legend in the order I want.

But is there something else I should be doing with col$output_set()?

regards - David
